“As long as the Iran conflict persists, markets will face the prospects of higher inflation, rate hikes, and tighter financial conditions,” said Vey-Sern Ling, a managing director at Union Bancaire Privee. “But investors should watch for buying opportunities with a longer-term view, given the depressed valuations this time, supported by surging AI-driven earnings.”

Some of the main moves in markets:
• The euro was little changed at US$1.1386
• The Japanese yen fell 0.3% to 157.80 per dollar
• The offshore yuan was little changed at 6.7170 per dollar
• The yield on 10-year Treasuries advanced four basis points to 5.20%

title: From geisha face paint to servers, Sakai Chemical emerges as AI linchpin
article:
(Sept 28): Sakai Chemical Industry Co’s century-old expertise in producing fine powders for face makeup used by geisha is finding a lucrative new use — powering the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.

Production capacity is quickly filling up at the Osaka-based company, which provides raw materials for capacitors necessary in AI data centres. Until recently, such production was a side business for Sakai Chemical, which has spent decades perfecting the production of ultra-fine and uniform particles — whether for safe, lead-free base material for traditional Japanese face powders, or for chemical compounds that store big electrical charges inside tiny components in servers.

The last year has transformed Sakai Chemical into a little-known tech supply chain linchpin. The company’s now calculating how much more production capability it needs to add, according to its president Toshiyuki Yagura.

A double-digit increase in manufacturing capacity is likely, according to Yagura. Advanced multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC) makers — such as clients Murata Manufacturing Co and Taiyo Yuden Co — raise their order forecasts at every meeting, he said. Sakai Chemical will make a decision regarding capex by March, he added.

“I didn’t think demand would grow this fast, and that’s all because of AI,” Yagura said in an interview, adding that he fields wistful jokes about the possibility of Sakai Chemical building facilities next to MLCC makers’ factories. The pace of AI-led momentum has eased somewhat, but he said the boom will likely last through 2027 at least.

Last quarter, Sakai Chemical’s electronics materials segment profit rose 22%, even as company-wide operating profit fell 10%, hurt by weak demand for building materials in Japan and changing trends in the sunscreen market. Electronics materials are now the company’s largest profit generator, surpassing its mainstay plastic additives business. The company’s stock price is up about 15% this year.

See also: Microsoft abandons personal AI chatbot race with Copilot reboot

The 108-year-old company started out by supplying high-purity zinc oxide as a safe alternative to the white lead historically used in the iconic makeup of geisha and kabuki entertainers. The older form of makeup provided a smooth, brilliant and long-lasting white finish, but caused chronic lead poisoning in Japan’s artist class. Sakai Chemical offered a safe material that offered white, opaque coverage that spread easily over the skin. From makeup, Sakai Chemical soon expanded into materials used in products ranging from sunscreens and car tyres to plastics and barium compounds.

The AI spending rush has put a spotlight on the company’s expertise in barium titanate, a critical chemical compound needed to make MLCCs — tiny components that regulate power flow in electronics. High-end capacitors used in AI servers need to be made from ultra-fine, uniform and high-purity barium titanate particles.

Sakai Chemical has been supplying the material for decades, but sales only began surging late last year, when annual orders for some products doubled as the AI infrastructure boom fuelled demand.

See also: When AI writes its own audit trail

While MLCC manufacturers also make the ingredient by mixing, firing and grinding barium and titanium compounds, they turn to Sakai Chemical for the materials needed to make capacitors for AI servers, according to Yagura. To make its ultra-pure powder, Sakai Chemical makes the compounds react in a liquid solution while exposing them to high temperature and pressure — a difficult process that requires precise control of multiple variables.

Despite high demand and insufficient capacity, the company has no plans to raise prices of its MLCC particles beyond what’s required to cover higher input costs, according to Yagura. That’s even as he acknowledges such reluctance weighs on corporate value.

“We are modest but proud of doing things right,” Yagura said.

Chinese manufacturers are spending heavily to catch up in chips, semiconductor materials and MLCCs. While Chinese companies’ market presence is growing in electronic materials, Japanese manufacturers retain an edge in consistency, Yagura said.

“Chinese makers may be able to show off their best samples out of their labs, but consistently delivering products of reliable quality is something Japan excels at,” he said.

title: Global funds end underweight position on China after four years
article:
(Sept 28): Global fund managers are dialing back their long-running retreat from Chinese stocks, drawn by AI prospects and favourable valuations.

Of nearly 2,800 global funds analysed by Bank of America, active long-only funds have, on average, moved to a “benchmark-neutral” weighting on China starting June, ending a four-year run of being “underweight,” according to its strategist Nigel Tupper. The funds collectively manage $562 billion in Chinese stocks.

The shift shows funds are encouraged by attractive valuations and improving profit outlooks in growth sectors like artificial intelligence. While it doesn’t necessarily signal a broad bullish turn, it indicates managers are largely done cutting their exposure, removing a major hurdle for the market’s recovery.

“Selling pressure is nearing a floor, shifting investor focus from positioning to earnings delivery,” Gary Tan, a portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, said, adding his firm is selectively adding Chinese stocks. “China does not need global investors to turn outright bullish for the market backdrop to improve; it may simply need them to stop cutting exposure.”

Other flow data point to a similar direction. Exchange-traded funds focused on China and Hong Kong drew US$19 million in August after US$1.94 billion of outflows in July, according to Bloomberg Intelligence’s (BI) data. Meanwhile, outflows from emerging-market funds that exclude China have been rising.

See also: Geely to buy 30% stake in Rival Nio’s battery-swapping unit

“China’s systematic ETF underweight is likely approaching a floor after the sharpest allocation reduction among major emerging markets,” said BI analyst Rebecca Sin. “The forces creating China’s underweight have started to lose momentum.”

Valuations may be helping. The MSCI China Index is trading at about 10.2 times 12-month forward earnings, below its 10-year average of 11.7 times.

See also: US releases product lists for US$30 bil China tariff deal

Investors are also finding improving earnings in parts of the market tied to Beijing’s technology ambitions. Shanghai-listed companies posted a 17.6% rise in first-half net income, according to Shanghai Securities News, driven by tech hardware and new-economy companies even as property and consumer industries lagged.

That divergence also means China’s market recovery remains uneven. The CSI 300 has fallen about 11% this quarter, and investors remain selective about where they put money.

“You buy the future of China,” Herald van der Linde, head of equity strategy for Asia Pacific at HSBC Holdings Plc, said, citing hardware technology and biopharma as preferred sectors. Consumer industries and real estate are “the past of China.”

title: Geely to buy 30% stake in Rival Nio’s battery-swapping unit
article:
(Sept 28): Zhejiang Geely Holding Group Co will buy a 30% stake in rival electric carmaker Nio Inc’s battery swapping unit for 640 million yuan (US$95 million), providing support for a cash intensive technology that Nio has been spearheading.

Geely will also include 100% equity interest of a battery swapping subsidiary as well as 640 million yuan in cash for the stake in Nio Power. The deal values Nio Power at 16 billion yuan, according to a statement on Monday.

The partnership comes as Nio continues to look for ways to further commercialise its battery swapping business. The technology is a unique selling point for its electric vehicles where drivers can replace a depleted battery with a charged one in a few minutes, but requires heavy investment and operational costs to build and maintain swapping stations. Contemporary Amperex Technology Co Ltd invested 2.5 billion yuan into Nio Power last year in a collaboration to build out a battery swapping network across China.

title: HSBC makes big push for affluent clients in India to fuel growth
article:
(Sept 28): HSBC Holdings plc is aiming to challenge India’s private-sector banks, betting that the country’s swelling pool of affluent customers and globally connected citizens can fuel its next phase of growth as it pushes deeper into smaller cities.

The London-based lender is doubling down in the world’s fastest-growing major economy across three areas — wealth, transaction banking and what Hitendra Dave, HSBC’s India chief executive officer, calls “globality”, — using its international network to cater to clients whose businesses and wealth span borders.

“Our ambition is to become one of the top four or five private banks in India by 2030,” the Mumbai-based executive said in an interview, referring to the wealth management business.

The growth drive puts HSBC in more direct competition with larger local rivals including ICICI Bank Ltd and Kotak Mahindra Ltd for a slice of India’s fast-expanding wealth pool. Still, the market is tricky to navigate as domestic banks are scaling up while firms founded by senior bankers are fighting for clients and talent, helping drive pay for relationship managers to record highs.

HSBC, Standard Chartered plc and Barclays plc are among a relatively small group of foreign banks building out their wealth management businesses in India, even as some global lenders have pulled back. Citigroup Inc sold its Indian consumer banking unit to Axis Bank Ltd, while Kotak agreed this year to acquire Deutsche Bank AG’s retail and wealth management businesses in India. Foreign lenders also face tighter restrictions on opening branches than their domestic rivals, making it harder to build nationwide networks.

The UK lender’s push comes as group chief executive officer Georges Elhedery said in a recent interview that the bank plans to increase investments in India, with a growing focus on affluent customers.

See also: ANZ bankers in Hong Kong, Singapore, Australia to exit in revamp — Bloomberg

The firm plans to expand to 46 branches across 34 cities in India over the next two years, from 34 branches currently, taking it further in smaller places. New locations include Bhubaneswar in the east, Rajkot in the west, Jalandhar in the north and Mysuru in the south. Standard Chartered has the largest network among foreign banks in the country, with 80 branches.

“We are building a wealth franchise beyond India’s metro cities,” said Dave, pointing to the growing number of wealthy individuals in smaller centres. HSBC’s private bank generally targets customers with at least US$2 million (RM8.17 million) in investable assets.

Dave described the next generation of Indian wealth as increasingly ‘global’, as more Indians study and work overseas, build international businesses and invest globally. “We can be especially valuable to customers whose financial lives, businesses and wealth cross borders,” he said.

See also: DBS seeks better AI returns by matching models to tasks

The firm’s expansion is already paying dividends. HSBC recently emerged as the biggest lender to India’s vast diaspora under a special foreign-exchange swap programme, disbursing US$10.9 billion from GIFT City in three months. ICICI Bank ranked second with US$8.4 billion.

HSBC is also using premium credit cards and large-ticket mortgages to deepen relationships with wealthy customers. Annual fees on its premium cards can run as high as 110,000 rupees (US$1,147 or RM4,685), while its mortgage book has tripled over the past four years.

Outstanding mortgages rose 25% from a year earlier to 257 billion rupees as of March 31, according to the bank as it focused on larger loans for premium homes. Transaction banking is another pillar of the strategy, with the lender helping companies process payroll, make foreign-exchange payments, distribute dividends and manage liquidity, Dave said.

title: CDL shares swoon to six-week low after $6 bil divestment target news
article:
Shares in City Developments (CDL) fell at open from $8.25 to an intra-day low of $7.74 before recovering to $7.91 as at 10.08am on Sept 28. The property group’s stock swooned following its pre-market announcement that it would divest $6 billion of assets while deploying $5 billion into Singapore, China, Japan and other markets.

CDL shares erased around six weeks’ worth of gains after the group released the outcome of its year-long strategic review, which group CEO Sherman Kwek first announced in February.

CDL is the day’s biggest loser, sinking the most out of the 30-stock Straits Times Index bellwether index as at 10am on Sept 28.

CDL is targeting $6 billion of divestments across the residential, commercial, hospitality and living sectors while deploying $5 billion of growth capital across the four sectors.

Nearly half (45%) of the targeted asset divestment mix will come from commercial properties. Hospitality assets are targeted to make up 30% of divestments, while legacy residential and other sectors will make up one-fifth of the $6 billion target and living sector assets will make up 5%.

See also: CDL targets $6 bil of divestments, aims to deploy $5 bil mostly in Singapore

Under a three-year refreshed strategy named GET+, CDL will also optimise its global hospitality portfolio of 165 hotels with around 48,000 rooms, including 88 owned hotels. Of these, 54 hotels (including two opening in the next 12 months) are directly held by CDL and valued at approximately $8.6 billion.

CDL says it will retain core assets but target approximately $1.8 billion of hotel divestments through FY2029, representing 30% of its $6 billion divestment target.

Singapore will remain the principal market for new investments, according to CDL. The group has shared a 60%-30%-10% breakdown for new investments across Singapore, China and Japan, and other markets respectively.

See also: Incredible Holdings seeks to be placed under judicial management

In addition to the divestment proceeds, the group expects more than $6 billion of projected cash inflows through to FY2029 from property development sales, supported by future cash collections from contracted sales and its existing development pipeline.

CDL will also establish a dedicated fund management entity, as the group aims to double assets under management (AUM) from $5 billion as of June 30 to $10 billion by FY2029.

The group says the fund management platform will create “a proprietary pipeline of opportunities” that can be seeded from CDL’s portfolio or new acquisitions and scaled with third-party capital.

Together, the group’s “four targeted measurable outcomes” include $1 billion in patmi to be realised from divestment gains, a net gearing target of around 55% by FY2029, a 35% or higher dividend payout ratio on reported patmi annually and $10 billion in AUM.

CDL will hold a briefing for media and analysts later today.

CDL shares closed 0.5% higher at $8.26 on Sept 25. CDL shares had surged past $10 in February in the lead up to the release of its FY2025 results.

title: Oil, AI demand give ringgit room to rally, strategists say
article:
(Sept 28): The Malaysian ringgit may be poised for gains as higher oil prices and the artificial-intelligence boom provide tailwinds for the currency, strategists say.

While the ringgit has declined 1.2% in September, lagging all Asian peers, MUFG Bank expects it to strengthen to 4.03 per dollar by year-end. Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp sees it at 4.0.

The ringgit closed 0.3% higher at 4.0738 per dollar on Friday.

A renewed climb in oil prices may bolster revenues for the energy exporting country, while Malaysia’s growing role in the AI supply chain gives it exposure to rising demand for semiconductors. With the political risk premium around some state elections also fading, strategists expect the ringgit to resume its advance.

“We could see a relief rally in the ringgit towards the year-end as macro environment concerns ease,” said Jeff Ng, head of Asia macro strategy at Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp in Singapore. “Malaysia’s overall fundamentals are still positive,” given its energy and electronic exports, as well as linkages to a stronger Chinese yuan, he said.

See also: Penang E&E players face capacity crunch amid influx of orders

The country’s exports have surged more than 35% in each of the five months through August, boosted by shipments of electronic products including semiconductors. Export growth averaged about 6.7% in 2025. Malaysia is now one of the world’s four largest net exporters of AI-related hardware, alongside South Korea, Taiwan and Thailand, according to the International Monetary Fund.

“Malaysia’s electronics trade surplus has been able to help offset the higher oil import bill,” said Lloyd Chan, a foreign-exchange strategist at MUFG in Singapore. “We see scope for ringgit strength,” supported by attractive sovereign bond and ringgit valuations, he added.

The local currency’s real effective exchange rate is around 2% below the 20-year average, according to data from the Bank for International Settlements. Continued bond inflows may help underpin the ringgit.

See also: UWC’s downturn bet puts it in pole position for semiconductor front-end boom

Investors will be watching the S&P Malaysia manufacturing PMI print for September due Thursday for further signs of economic expansion, as the region continues to grapple with the fallout from the Middle East. Still, Malaysia may be better placed than some peers to weather higher energy costs as one of the world’s top exporters of liquefied natural gas.

“Malaysia has been on the right side of the terms-of-trade story throughout the year,” and is best-positioned to benefit from AI investment and higher energy prices, Goldman Sachs Group Inc strategists including Danny Suwanapruti wrote in a note on Sept 18. With the central bank turning slightly more hawkish, “the conditions are in place for ringgit to outperform,” they said, recommending a long ringgit/baht trade.

title: Low family controlling Hafary Holdings tables 64 cents privatisation offer
article:
The Low family controlling Hafary Holdings is making an offer of 64 cents per share to privatise the company.

They will not revise the offer, which is made via a vehicle called 23 Capital.

Together with an entity called Hap Seng Investment Holdings, the concerted parties already control 89.96% of the company, which is a supplier of building materials.

The offer of 64 cents is a premium of around 4.9% over the last transacted price per share on Sept 25.

As of June 30, Hafary's net asset value was 35.2 cents per share.

See also: Privatisation offer for Low Keng Huat raised to 78 cents per share

In the most recent half year ended June, the company reported earnings of $10.2 million, down 22.2% y-o-y. Revenue in the same period was down 10.5% to $122.7 million.

According to the offerors, Hafary has not raised capital from the market in the last decade and does not see itself doing so in the foreseeable future, as it can tap bank borrowings.

title: CDL targets $6 bil of divestments, aims to deploy $5 bil mostly in Singapore
article:

Nearly half (45%) of the targeted asset divestment mix will come from commercial properties. Singapore will remain the principal market for new investments, says CDL in a Sept 28 announcement.

Kwek Leng Beng, executive chairman of CDL, says: “For over six decades, CDL has built a strong and diversified real estate and hospitality portfolio supported by deep capabilities and quality assets. The strategic review builds on these strengths, while sharpening our priorities and setting a clear direction for the group.”

Sherman Kwek, group CEO of CDL, says: “GET+ marks our next chapter of value creation, with a three-year execution roadmap marked by a sharper focus around where we deploy capital, how we manage our portfolio and where we can unlock value. Through the 3-4-5-6 roadmap and measurable outcomes, we have provided greater accountability for what we need to deliver and our unwavering focus will be on strong execution as we work to strengthen our balance sheet, improve capital productivity and build a higher-quality earnings base to maximise shareholder value.”

CDL will hold a briefing for media and analysts later today.

The junior Kwek first announced the review on Feb 27 during the group’s results presentation for FY2025 ended Dec 31, 2025. He added that the group had engaged a global advisory firm, later revealed to be Teneo, to spearhead the review.

At the group’s 1HFY2026 results briefing in August, the junior Kwek said the review will include a “very concrete plan” that was backed by assets and numbers to lower its gearing to a level that he thinks everybody “should be very happy with”.

CDL shares closed 0.5% higher at $8.26 on Sept 25. CDL shares had surged past $10 in February in the lead up to the release of its FY2025 results.

title: Stoneweg Europe Stapled Trust proposes to internalise manager and operating platform
article:
Stoneweg Europe Stapled Trust is proposing to internalise the REIT manager, trustee-manager of the business trust and the pan-European logistics and light-industrial platform that manages SERT’s assets and selected third-party asset management contracts.

This follows an Aug 13 announcement where SERT said it was in discussions with its sponsor, SWI Group, regarding “a range of initiatives aimed at enhancing long-term value for stapled securityholders” including a proposed internalisation of the REIT manager and trustee-manager.

In SERT’s Sept 28 announcement, the trust says the transaction will create a platform with EUR3.2 billion ($4.7 billion) of assets under management (AUM), including SERT’s existing EUR2.3 billion portfolio and third-party asset management contracts totalling EUR820 million.

Along with the proposed internalisation, SERT will enter into two strategic cooperation agreements with with sponsor, SWI Group, which owns a 28% stake in SERT’s stapled securities and wholly owns the manager and property manager.

Operating as an independent and internally manager platform will allow SERT to benefit from “exclusive logistics and light industrial investment rights across Europe and, through these agreements, preferred access to SWI Group’s specialist data centre capabilities and opportunities,” says the trust.

The purchase consideration for the proposed internalisation is EUR114 million and the effective consideration is EUR94 million. Both figures exclude the co-investment stakes related to third-party asset management contracts. The difference reflects a benefit arising from the 40 million subscription securities issued to SWI Group at EUR2 per security, which is a 33% premium to the volume-weighted average trading price of around EUR1.50 as at Sept 24.

See also: Keppel REIT to divest T Tower at agreed property value of 348.8 bil won

The EUR2 issue price only applies to the one-off subscription by SWI and does not constitute a capital raise from existing securityholders.

The proposed internalisation will be funded through EUR80 million from SWI Group’s subscription for 40 million new SERT stapled securities and up to EUR34 million in cash payable by the trust. A further EUR8.4 million in cash may be paid for co-investment stakes linked to third-party asset management contracts that transfer to SERT by completion.

See also: MLT to divest property in Shanghai, China for RMB323 mil, extends lease at 201 Keppel Road for another nine months

The proposed internalisation will bring together 100 employees across 10 European jurisdictions and Singapore, who currently manage SERT’s 96 assets.

According to the managers, the proposed internalisation is expected to be accretive to SERT’s distribution per stapled security (DPS) by 5.9%, or 14.18 Euro cents on an FY2025 pro forma basis, up from 13.39 Euro cents.

The accretion is supported by earnings generated by the acquired management and operating platform, including other institutional asset management contracts and the EUR20 million adjustment to the consideration from SWI Group’s subscription.

SERT also noted other benefits including its securityholders benefitting from its platform earnings and future growth, noting a net uplift to distributable income of EUR10.1 million based on FY2025 fees paid to the sponsor.

Third-party asset management contracts, which generate recurring fee income, also create a broader earnings platform, while the agreements with sponsor SWI Group preserves SERT’s access to “future growth opportunities”.

Lim Swe Guan, chair and non-independent non-executive director of the manager, called the proposed internalisation a “landmark transaction” and a “deliberate step toward building a resilient, transparent and sustainably managed platform that delivers superior risk-adjusted returns to our securityholders over time”.

Max-Hervé George, founder & CEO of SWI Group added that the internalisation is a “milestone that cements its position as our flagship European logistics and light industrial vehicle – independently managed while remaining strategically connected to our global network, while SWI Group's team efforts will be concentrating on digital infrastructure.”

Jaume Sabater, founder & CEO of Stoneweg Group noted that the transaction marked a “natural evolution” of the REIT and sponsor’s partnership and said SWI Group will remain a long-term strategic investor of the trust.

“SERT is building on a strong foundation forged over nine years of proven track record and demonstrated resilience. Its long-term business performance is anchored by the REIT, which continues to deliver stable and growing distributions to securityholders, while the business trust and earnings from the acquired asset management platform provide additional sources of growth beyond the core portfolio,” says Simon Garing, CEO of the manager.

“Our two strategic cooperation agreements with SWI Group complement the proposed internalisation by preserving strategic access to logistics and data centre opportunities, maintaining SERT's independence as a fully internally managed platform and supporting continued growth in the logistics, light industrial and digital infrastructure sectors,” he adds.

The proposed internalisation and strategic cooperation agreements are subject to regulatory approvals, securityholders' approval at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) and other customary closing conditions. A circular together with a notice of the EGM will be issued, says SERT.

Units in SERT closed 5 Euro cents lower or 3.36% down at EUR1.44 while its SGD counter closed 7 cents lower or 3.23% down at $2.10 on Sept 25.

title: Mainboard-listed Oiltek submits application for Bursa Malaysia listing
article:
In a bourse filing on Sept 28, Mainboard-listed Oiltek International has announced that it has submitted an application for a secondary listing on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia on Sept 25. The application has been submitted by M & A Securities, Oiltek’s principal advisor, to the Securities Commission (SC) Malaysia.

First announced in July 2025, the secondary listing will comprise a public offering and a private placement of new shares. In addition, there will be a private placement for existing shares. The private placements are for Bumiputera investors approved by Malaysia’s Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry.

The final structure, size and issue/offer price of the new listing will be determined at a later date and will be announced in due course, says Oiltek. The listing will remain subject to, among others, the approvals of the SC, Bursa Securities, Bank Negara Malaysia, MITI and such other relevant authorities as may be required.

Upon receiving approval by the relevant authorities for the new listing, Oiltek will be convening an EGM to seek shareholders approval for constitution amendment, a proposed bonus shares issue for entitled shareholders and new shares issue for the Malaysian listing.

The company reported a decrease in net profit after tax (npat) of 6.9% y-o-y to RM13.2 ($4.15) million for 1HFY2026 ended June 30, with RM99.2 million in revenue, down 1.6% y-o-y from the previous corresponding period.

Shares in Oiltek closed at $1.25 on Sept 25. Ytd, the stock is up 78%.

title: Great Eastern Holdings appoints former ComfortDelGro director to its board
article:
Great Eastern Holdings has appointed Adeline Sum Wai Fun as an non-executive and independent director of the board.

Sum, whose appointment will take effect from Oct 1, will also be appointed as a member of Great Eastern’s audit committee on the same day.

According to the insurer, Sum possesses the “requisite experience and expertise” which would enable her to contribute to the effectiveness of the board.

Sum was previously an independent non-executive director of ComfortDelGro, where she served for 16 years - from Jan 1, 2007, to April 28, 2023. She retired from the role at the group’s annual general meeting (AGM) in April 2023.

Her previous careers include being the CEO of the Singapore Labour Foundation from January 2019 to June 2025 and CEO of NTUC Enterprise Co-operative Limited from October 2023 to March 2026.

title: Oil rises as Iran says it won’t soften Strait of Hormuz demands
article:
(Sept 28): Oil rose as Iran stuck to a seven-day proposal for reopening the crucial Strait of Hormuz rejected by US President Donald Trump, threatening further delays in the reopening of the crucial waterway.

Brent advanced above US$106 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate headed toward US$94. Tehran’s conditions are something Washington might have agreed to about a year ago, Trump told Axios in an interview on Sunday, saying that Iran has overplayed its hand. The US president said he expects negotiations to resume this week, Axios said.

Oil prices swung last week on mixed signals over diplomacy, recovering Middle East flows and uncertainty over US measures to curb record diesel prices, which Trump said Washington is looking at “very seriously.” Brent is up more than 70% this year, and on track for its third monthly gain, as the US-Iran conflict enters its eight month, adding to inflationary pressures.

Traders will continue to monitor physical flows through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world’s crude and liquefied natural gas before the start of the conflict. Trump said a “record amount” of oil was taken out of the strait on Saturday night, while the Fars news agency reported Iranian forces targeted ships using unauthorized routes through the waterway.

Regional tensions also remain elevated. Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said on Saturday that air defenses intercepted Houthi drones headed toward Riyadh and a missile targeting Khamis Mushait in the south. Alerts were also issued at Abha and Jazan, which host Aramco’s energy facilities.
